ops.title: fusekit: tune the three load-sensitive tests exposed by the macOS CI move
ops.description: The F0 CI restructure (2026-08-03) moved fusekit's suite from 8 dedicated ubuntu runners to 4 shared macOS shards, and three tests turned load-sensitive: the two pre-diagnosed deadline assertions (catalog io_concurrency, catalogservice runtime_broker — tuned on faster ubuntu runners) plus a third found on the first real run: holder's TestRuntimeOwnerRecoveryIDFollowsImmutableSourceCapability/empty_source-capable_owner, a subprocess-spawn + async-readiness race that transitioned the runtime to Failed/Draining at 3s against a 30s budget (triage on run 30793955106: real fork/exec timing sensitivity exposed by 4-way shared-runner contention; the shard scripts themselves were ruled out). Candidate fixes: derive readiness margins from a measured baseline, or serialize the subprocess-spawning readiness tests within a shard. Rides naturally with the F2-F6 migration wave, which touches holder's readiness path anyway.

ops.text: catalog/io_concurrency_test.go:35, catalogservice/runtime_broker_test.go:1612, and holder TestRuntimeOwnerRecoveryIDFollowsImmutableSourceCapability/empty_source-capable_owner survive 5 consecutive macOS CI runs without a flake
The fix is margin-derivation or serialization of subprocess-spawning readiness tests — not a blind timeout bump without a rationale
